attributes.description: Fires when the PostgreSQL availability gauge reports 0 for a Supabase project, meaning the exporter could not reach the database. Every other service in the project is a client of this database, so this is the highest-priority signal.
attributes.name: [Supabase OTel] PostgreSQL is down

investigation_guide.blob:
## PostgreSQL Down

A Supabase project is a small fleet of services (PostgREST, Auth/GoTrue, Realtime, the poolers) sharing one PostgreSQL instance. When `pg_up` reads 0 the whole project is effectively unavailable.

### Triage Steps
1. Confirm the database is genuinely down rather than the exporter being broken. If the `[Supabase OTel] Metrics collection is failing` rule is also active, suspect the collector first.
2. Check whether the database bounced rather than stopped: `TS metrics-supabase.metrics.otel-* | STATS restarts = SUM(INCREASE(postgresql_restarts_total)) BY resource.attributes.supabase_project_ref`
3. Check the host for the cause: a full or read-only data volume, or an OOM kill, will all stop PostgreSQL.
4. Check whether the connection budget was exhausted immediately before the outage — the exporter's own connection can be refused when `max_connections` is reached.

### Escalation
This is a full project outage. Escalate immediately.

### Tuning
`MIN()` is used across series so one unhealthy scrape target is not masked by a healthy one. If the metric is absent entirely the query returns no rows and the rule stays silent, so a project that does not expose `pg_up` never produces a false alert.
